description.purpose: The fan-out half of a tool loop: one code cell that splits a brain's tool_call bundle into one routable message per call, announces the round to the fan-in first, and passes a final answer through. It carries no map of the topology -- a call leaves as a NAME plus its call id, and the edges of the tree decide which cell that name is.
description.use_when: Between an agent's llm cell and its tools, next to a collector that does the fan-in. Wire the four exit routes in the SAME mutation that instantiates it: 'calls' and 'result' into the collector, one edge per tool on hop.tool_name, 'answer' onto the reply path.
description.not_in_scope: No fan-in, no tool execution, no argument validation, no iteration counting. The loop bound and restore_ttl belong on the re-entry edge (GH #82), not in this cell. A tool name with no edge is a routing error by design, not something the cell resolves.
examples: PORTS - Entry: the llm cell's output (hop.finish_reason). Exit on hop.route: 'calls' -> the collector's in_calls port, 'tool' -> the tool cells, selected by `has(hop.tool_name) && hop.tool_name == '<name>'`, 'result' -> the collector's in_tool port (synthetic errors only), 'answer' -> the collector's in_answer port or the reply sink.
a two-tool round: web_search and web_fetch are asked in one answer, run in parallel, and both results reach the fan-in under the ids the split preserved
a brain that asks for 40 tools at once: DISPATCHER_MAX_CALLS refuses the bundle as a whole and answers all 40 ids with 'call budget exceeded', so the agent replies instead of stalling
